sentences.text: Ningyuansaurus belongs to the pennaraptoran group of dinosaurs.
This animal possessed eyes that were notably large.
Its head was triangular and extended further than seen in most early oviraptorosaurs, with a straight lower jaw.
The forelimbs were short, where the upper arm bones exceeded the length of the lower arm bones.
Legs were elongated, with the thigh bone measuring longer than the pelvic bones.
A lengthy tail ended with impressions of feathers.
The sole known species, Ningyuansaurus wangi, comes from one fossil found in the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of western Liaoning Province, China.
The specific name 'wangi' commemorates Wang Qiuwu, the private collector who donated the remains.
Today, the specimen resides in the Confuciusornis Museum in Xingcheng.
The fossil dates to roughly 124.6 million years ago within the Aptian stage.
Estimates place the animal's existence between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago, covering the Barremian to Aptian stages.
Although initially considered the most basal oviraptorosaur, subsequent studies reclassified it as part of Halszkaraptorinae.
Phylogenetic analyses by Cau and Madzia (2021) situated Ningyuansaurus in various locations within the dinosaur family tree.
